answer: I would like to talk about someone very close to home. The person who has influenced me most is my father, who ran a small business in Sirajganj for over thirty years and has only recently retired. Obviously I have known him all my life, but I think I only really started to understand him as a teenager, when I began helping out in his shop after school. Growing up, I watched him deal with setbacks that would have [[discouraged]] most people, yet he always stayed calm and kept going. There were slow seasons, especially during the monsoon, when hardly anyone came in, but he never let his worries spill over into family life. What shaped me was not any single piece of advice, but the quiet example he set day after day. He treated every customer, however difficult, with the same [[integrity]], and he taught me that a good reputation is built slowly and lost quickly. When I was struggling to choose a career, he never pushed me in one direction; instead he encouraged me to be [[self-reliant]] and make my own decisions. Looking back, almost everything I value about hard work and honesty can be traced to him, and I try to bring the same patience to my job at the consultancy, especially with anxious students. His influence has been [[profound]], and I still catch myself asking what he would do in a tricky situation. In many ways he remains my quiet role model, even now that I am an adult, and I suspect he always will be.

followUps.q: Do you still ask your father for advice?
followUps.answer: Yes, quite often, especially about money or big decisions. Since he retired he has more time to talk, so we usually chat over tea in the evening, and his advice is still remarkably [[level-headed]].

followUps.q: Would you like to be like him in the future?
followUps.answer: In many ways, yes. I would love to have his patience and honesty, although I probably will not run a shop. I just hope people eventually see me as someone as trustworthy as he is.
